title: Cold-start warmup capacity budgeting profiles - Q3 2026
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a proposal for operationalizing warmup / cold-start capacity budgets across regions to reduce tail latency during failover and scale events. The goal is to define deterministic pre-warm pool targets, staggered warmup sequencing, and cost-aware budget envelopes for multi-region redundancy drills and unexpected surge absorbtion.

Scope:
- Multi-region: us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1, ap-southeast1.
- GPU types: H100 (primary for high-throughput), A100 (fallback / spot-like), T4 for smaller low-latency endpoints.
- Workloads: hosted-api text-gen heavy (seq=1024 median), chat sessions (avg seq=512, KV caching used), embedding requests (short seq).

High-level assumption summary (conservative defaults for planning):
- Peak global QPS (hosted): 14k req/s.
- Peak regional split assumption under failure: worst-case all traffic to one region multiplier = 2.5x local baseline.
- Avg tokens per request: 650 tokens (text-gen), 120 tokens (chat), 25 tokens (embeddings).
- Token throughput per GPU (H100, mixed precision, optimized kernels): 12k tokens/s (steady), 3k tokens/s cold start warmup ramp.
- Warmup ramp time (no prewarm): 6–12 minutes to reach full per-GPU throughput; with prewarm pools targeted, <30s tail at p95.

Key definitions used here:
- Prewarm pool: fraction of GPUs kept in a ready state (model loaded and KV cache warm) to absorb traffic spikes with minimal latency impact.
- Warmup budget: reserved GPU count dedicated to prewarm across regions (can be dynamic on schedule).
- Cold-start window: the time needed to reach steady-state throughput for a newly started GPU serving large sequence requests.

Budgeting methodology (formulae):
- RequiredTokensPerSecond = regional_peak_qps * avg_tokens_per_request
- BaselineGpusNeeded = ceil(RequiredTokensPerSecond / tokens_per_gpu_steady)
- PrewarmTarget = ceil(BaselineGpusNeeded * prewarm_fraction)
- StagedWarmupPlan: kickoff N_prewarm first, then N_incremental every Xs until Baseline achieved.

Conservative safety knobs:
- prewarm_fraction = 0.10 (10%) for normal SLOs; 0.20 for critical enterprise customers or during black-swan drills.
- safety_factor = 1.15 (15%) applied to BaselineGpusNeeded for headroom during model degradation or slower kernels.

Example region-level calculation (scenario: eu-west1 receives redirected traffic during a us outage):
- Observed eu-west1 baseline QPS: 1,800 req/s -> worst-case redirected factor 2.5 => regional_peak_qps = 4,500 req/s.
- Weighted avg tokens: assume 70% text-gen (650), 25% chat (512), 5% embedding (25) => avg_tokens_per_request = round(0.7*650 + 0.25*512 + 0.05*25) = ~582 tokens.
- RequiredTokensPerSecond = 4,500 * 582 = 2,619,000 tokens/s.
- tokens_per_gpu_steady (H100) = 12,000 tokens/s -> BaselineGpusNeeded = ceil(2,619,000 / 12,000) = 219 GPUs.
- Apply safety_factor 1.15 -> 252 GPUs.
- PrewarmTarget @10% -> 26 GPUs kept warm in eu-west1.

Staging plan (fast absorb):
- Stage 0 (steady): 26 prewarmed GPUs hot, 226 standby cold.
- Stage 1 (initial surge, 0–30s): distribute incoming load to 26 prewarm GPUs -> expected token capacity = 26 * 12k = 312k tokens/s which covers ~53% of the immediate requirement; remaining traffic queued/buffered to autoscaler.
- Stage 2 (30s–3min): spin up additional 80 GPUs (fast boot group, model cached on image) to cover 312k + 80*12k = 1,272k tokens/s.
- Stage 3 (3–10min): remaining GPUs ramp to the full 252 target.

Cost / capacity tradeoffs (back-of-envelope):
- On-demand H100 hourly cost assumed: $4.50 / GPU-hour (internal blended).
- Prewarm pool cost for eu-west1 = 26 * 24 * $4.50 = $2,808 / day.
- If prewarm_fraction increased to 20%, daily cost doubles but p95 cold-start tail drops significantly.

Operational playbook (for SRE / Duty):
- Pre-declare windows: enable elevated prewarm_fraction for scheduled product launches and known regulatory failovers (toggle via infra-config).
- Canary routing: when shifting traffic, route 10% to target region for 2 minutes, observe token backpressure and latency curves, then ramp.
- Auto-rollback: if target region p95 latency > SLO for 3 consecutive samples, fallback traffic to next region and trigger incident.

Automation heuristics to consider (implementation TODOs):
- AdaptivePrewarm controller: increase prewarm_fraction when 7-day trend of tail latency or token-per-request increases by >15%.
- RapidBootstrap images: maintain pre-baked container image with model shard + boot scripts to reduce cold startup by 40–60%.
- KV warm transfer: allow KV snapshot import upon startup from remote peers to reduce warmup from minutes to seconds (privacy/consistency caveats).

Failure cases and mitigations matrix (short):
- Region network partition (upstream): increase local prewarm to 20% and enable routing to secondaries.
- Image pull storm: maintain small local registry mirror prepopulated with latest runtime images in each region.
- Autoscaler rate limit: allow burst buffer token queue at edge gateways for up to 45s to smooth spikes.

DR drill checklist (runbook skeleton):
1) Notify SRE + On-call + Product incident lead.
2) Increase prewarm_fraction to 20% in target region via infra toggle (should take <60s to flip).
3) Open canary 10% traffic for 2m; monitor p50/p95/p99 and token backlog metric.
4) If metrics within thresholds, ramp to 50% for 3m, then full re-route.
5) If regressions, redirect to third region and file postmortem.

Open items / investigation tasks (short list):
- Measure actual tokens_per_gpu_steady for our most-used models under 1k seq and 2k seq (test matrix).
- Prototype KV snapshot import (Priya to lead; infra ticket JIRA-10112).
- Simulate failover scenario with synthetic traffic to validate 10% prewarm target effectiveness across 4 regions (Miguel to run).
- Quantify cost delta for 10% vs 20% prewarm across calendar month windows (Liam to run extended simulation).

Notes / stray thoughts (working doc style):
- Consider using cheaper GPU classes for prewarm (A100-40GB) if model quantized enough; saves cost but increases fallback complexity.
- Time-of-day scheduling: prewarm_fraction can be lowered off-peak to save cost and increase before known windows (marketing events).
- Keep this sheet as the canonical quick-runbook for cold-start budgeting; convert to Confluence once validated.

Appendix: brief scenario table (rounded numbers)
- us-west1 baseline QPS 4,000 -> peak redirected 10,000 -> tokens/sec ~6.1M -> baseline GPUs ~508 -> safety 585 -> prewarm 59 (10%)
- us-east1 baseline QPS 3,200 -> peak redirected 8,000 -> tokens/sec ~4.66M -> baseline GPUs ~389 -> safety 447 -> prewarm 45
- eu-west1 (example above) -> baseline 1,800 -> peak 4,500 -> prewarm 26
- ap-southeast1 baseline QPS 600 -> peak 1,500 -> prewarm 9

Quick glossary for on-call:
- "prewarm_fraction" = configuration key infra.prewarm_fraction (0.0 - 1.0).
- "fast_boot_group" = instance class with pre-installed cached image.
- "KV snapshot" = ephemeral cache state transfer used to reduce model context warmup.

End of working sheet.
(Will iterate with simulation outputs and actual bench numbers; mark as draft until validated.)
